references.text: Jesus had settled in Capernaum and performed miracles there, which the people of Nazareth had heard about and referred to.
The rumor about Jesus had spread throughout the region, explaining why the people of Nazareth had heard of his deeds in Capernaum.
Jesus responds to the proverb "Physician, heal yourself" with another saying that no prophet is accepted in his hometown—both address Nazareth's expectations and rejection.
John mentions that Jesus went to Capernaum, confirming that he performed miracles there before coming to Nazareth.
One of the miracles Jesus performed near Capernaum, which the people of Nazareth may have heard about.
The parallel in Matthew where Jesus is rejected in his hometown of Nazareth, and the people take offense at him because they know his background.
The parallel in Mark where Jesus visits his hometown and is not recognized there—a prophet without honor in his own land.
Also in John, the people question Jesus' origin and identity, similar to the skepticism he encountered in Nazareth.
